applicability_domain.kind: OLS leverage vs warning leverage h* = 3p/n
applicability_domain.note: Leverage and the deck's 1-D training-range label can disagree for a ligand just outside the feature min/max; both are reported.

experimental_protocol.ee_to_ddG: Convert measured ee (fraction) to ddG = 2 R T atanh(ee) at T = 298.15 K, then compare to the interval above.
experimental_protocol.measurement: Run the asymmetric Ni-hDA reaction with each candidate ligand under the source conditions; determine product enantiomeric excess by chiral HPLC or SFC.
experimental_protocol.not_an_instruction: Candidates are computational recommendations; synthetic accessibility, stability, and safety require expert review.
experimental_protocol.source: Sigman Group, Ni-Catalyzed-hDA repository (https://github.com/SigmanGroup/Ni-Catalyzed-hDA); the univariate enantioselectivity model reproduced in StericX Study 001.

falsification_rule.corroborated_if: measured ddG within the 95% prediction interval for at least 6 of 8 primary candidates AND Spearman rho(predicted, measured) > 0
falsification_rule.honest_power_caveat: Near-racemate predictions have ee intervals spanning both signs and are not meaningfully falsifiable on ee; the ddG interval remains the test quantity.
falsification_rule.secondary_set: boundary-challenge ligands, scored as an extrapolation stress-test; reported but not gating the primary test

limitations: Ten training points; a univariate steric model of one reaction family.
Candidates are DFT-characterized, not necessarily synthesizable.
Must not be refit after any outcome is known.
reaction_source: Sigman Group, Ni-Catalyzed-hDA repository (https://github.com/SigmanGroup/Ni-Catalyzed-hDA); the univariate enantioselectivity model reproduced in StericX Study 001.
supersedes: adds an uncertainty/applicability-domain/protocol layer over the frozen deck; the point predictions are unchanged and verified byte-for-byte against it
